questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Dharampal will be remain in jail (1)/because of the other cases (2)/pending against him. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the tense should be formed correctly. The verbs have been used incorrectly.

The correct tense here would be simple future ‘will remain’ or future continuous tense ‘will be remaining.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

When he was arrested by the police (A)/ in November 2014, his followers go on (B)/ the rampage for two weeks. (C)/ No Error (D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2- B**

The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as the tense ‘go’ in simple present is incorrect. The whole sentence is structured in simple past tense so ‘went’ is the correct verb to be used here.

questions.question:

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Evoke
questions.solution: The word ‘evoke’ means ‘bring or recall (a feeling, memory, or image) to the conscious mind.’ The word ‘extract’ means ‘remove or take out, especially by effort or force.’ Thus ‘forget’ is the correct antonym.

questions.question:

Let's look at the meaning of the given word and the marked option:

Hence from the given meanings, we find that both the words express the opposite meaning.

Thus, the correct answer is Option 3 Disproportion. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50618910e2858de29bd243bf3e03a7eb28611b5a177e22623b53abcc6a893c97.png]

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Deplete
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e Expand 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52da89e0a2679b367562ad6c0d6e656a668762aeb60deda63544b7552771e3b0.png] Explanation

Let's look at the meaning of the given word and the marked option:

 
• Deplete: The word "deplete" means to use up or exhaust a resource or supply.

 
 
• For example, if you deplete your bank account, it means you have used up all the money in it.
 
 
 
• Similarly, if a natural resource like oil or water is depleted, it means that there is less of it available than there was before.
 
• The opposite of deplete would be to increase or add to something, rather than using it up or taking it away. 
 
• The word "**expand**" means to become larger in size or to increase in quantity, number, or scope.
 
 
• For example, if a business expands, it means that it is growing and adding new locations, products, or services.
 
 

Hence from the given meanings, we find that both words express the opposite meaning.

The other options, "empty", "lessen", and "waste" are all related to the idea of reducing or using up resources, and are therefore not opposites of "deplete".

Thus, the correct answer is Option 3 Expand

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50618910e2858de29bd243bf3e03a7eb28611b5a177e22623b53abcc6a893c97.png] 

Let's look at the meaning of the other given options:

 
• Empty: Containing nothing; not filled. 
 
• Lessen: Make or become less; diminish
 
• **Waste**: Use or expend carelessly.

questions.question:

We all believe that a slight elevation (in your) body temperature means we are getting sick.
questions.solution: The correct pronoun here should be ‘our’ as the sentence mentions ‘we’. Thus ‘your’ is incorrect here.

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

It is lowest in the morning and (little lesser) during late afternoon.
questions.solution: The correct form of the adjective should be written here. Since ‘lowest’ is the superlative form of the word the comparative form of the adjective which is ‘lower’ should be used here. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

A list and explanation of difficult words.
questions.solution:

Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Methane is another

P: greenhouse gas release in the

Q: atmosphere by the anaerobic

R: decomposition of organic materials
questions.solution: P is the first statement as it states what is methane. Q follows P as it states where it is released. R completes the sentence by mentioning the way of its release.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Education is an essential

P: get success in life and

Q: earn respect and recognition

R: tool for everyone to
questions.solution: R must be the first statement as the word ‘tool’ fits correctly after the adjective ‘essential.’ Since P ends with ‘and’ it must be the second statement and cannot be the third one. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: really tragic that in the ______ world
questions.solution: The word here must convey a positive meaning to portray the contradicting scenario. The word ‘tragic’ helps us to understand. The word ‘progressive’ means ‘advanced’ and fits here correctly. The word ‘regressive’ means ‘returning to a former or less developed state’ and does not fit here. The word ‘conclusive’ means ‘decisive’ and ‘inductive’ means ‘characterized by the inference of general laws from particular instances.’

questions.question: they are too poor to ______ a rich dowry.
questions.solution: The word ‘concord’ means ‘agreement or harmony between people or groups.’ The word ‘afford’ means ‘have enough money to pay for’ and fits here correctly. The word ‘discord’ means ‘disagreement between people’ and cannot fit here. The word ‘oxford’ means ‘a thick cotton fabric chiefly used to make shirts’ and is irrelevant here.

questions.question: her ______ worth used to be the primary
questions.solution: Here the correct adjective should be chosen for the word ‘worth.’ The word ‘immoral’ means ‘unethical’ and does not fit here. Option 2 does not fit here too. The word ‘moralistic’ means ‘over fond of making moral judgements about others' behaviour; too ready to moralize’ and is the correct word. The word ‘analgesic’ means ‘acting to relieve pain’ and does not convey any meaning here.

questions.question: dowry is the ______ and the only
questions.solution: The sentence conveys the significance of dowry thus the word ‘first’ is correct here. The word ‘penultimate’ means ‘last but one in a series of things; second last’ and does not fit here. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: has become a ______ of oppression
questions.solution: The word ‘cause’ means ‘reason’ and conveys correctly that dowry has become a reason of oppression. It is not a consequence soothe other options do not fit here. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.
